docs.title: Providing intel on cybersecurity risks across African continent and third world countries`
docs.text:
welcome to NetIris, your overview of everything cybersecurity.

As digital adoption grows, especially in mobile money and social media, cyber risks arent left behind. NetIris provides plain-language guides and aggregated threat data to help in understanding these threats and protect yourself.

docs.title: 1. Communications Authority of Kenya (National KE-CIRT/CC)
docs.text:
• Source Name: Communications Authority of Kenya (CA) / National KE-CIRT/CC
  • Report Title: Cyber Security Report Q1 2026-2027
  • Link: https://www.ca.go.ke/sites/default/files/2026-10Cyber%20Security%20Report%20Q1%202026-2027.pdf
  • Date Checked: November 2, 2026
  • License/Attribution: Public government report; requires attribution to the Communications Authority of Kenya.
  • Key Findings: Detected national cyber threat events rose by 14.45% in a single quarter (July–September 2026) to reach 2.696 billion. Social engineering, stolen credentials, and malicious links targeting mobile ecosystems drove a 34.43% surge in issued mobile threat advisories.

docs.title: 2. INTERPOL African Cyberthreat Assessment Report
docs.text:
• Source Name: INTERPOL Africa Cybercrime Operations Desk
  • Report Title: African Cyberthreat Assessment Report 2026
  • Link: https://www.interpol.int/Media/Documents/Publications/Cybercrime/African-Cyberthreat-Assessment-Report-2026
  • Date Checked: November 2, 2026
  • License/Attribution: Publicly available report; requires clear attribution to INTERPOL.
  • Key Findings: Generative AI tools are actively enabling up to 55% of all cybercrime across Africa. Social engineering, smishing (SMS phishing), and synthetic identity fraud are specifically targeting mobile financial services and public sector institutions.

docs.title: Understanding Smishing and Mobile Money Fraud
docs.text: Mobile money is a vital part of daily life across Africa. However, its rapid adoption has made it a primary target for cybercriminals. According to INTERPOL's 2026 African Cyberthreat Assessment Report, generative AI tools are now enabling up to 55% of all cybercrime across the continent. A significant portion of this activity involves smishing (SMS phishing) and synthetic identity fraud specifically targeting mobile financial services.

docs.title: How These Scams Work
docs.text: Criminals use AI to create highly convincing, personalized text messages that mimic official alerts from banks or mobile network operators. They often create a false sense of urgency, claiming your account is locked, a transaction failed, or you must verify your identity immediately.

docs.title: What to do: Protect your mobile money
docs.text: Never share your PIN or OTP: Legitimate organizations will never ask for your Personal Identification Number (PIN) or One-Time Password (OTP) via SMS or phone call. Verify independently: If you receive an urgent message, do not click any links. Open your mobile money app directly or call the official customer service number found on the back of your SIM card or the provider's official website. Report suspicious activity: Forward suspicious SMS messages to your mobile network provider's fraud hotline and report the incident to your national CERT (e.g., KE-CIRT/CC in Kenya)
